text: Setting clear goals is essential for any project's success. A useful framework is the SMART method, which means goals should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," a SMART goal would be "increase page load speed by 20% within three months." Once you have your main goal, break it into smaller milestones, such as completing a design draft or testing the new code. Each milestone should have clear deliverables, like a report or a working prototype, so you can track progress. It is also vital to ensure stakeholder alignment. This means regularly communicating with everyone involved, from team members to clients, to confirm they agree on the priorities and expectations. When everyone shares the same vision, the project runs more smoothly and avoids misunderstandings.
